kind_legend.accounting: A bookkeeping rule. Upgrades straight to verified by a controlled experiment; literature does not apply.
kind_legend.behaviour: A causal response (a lever moves demand, retention ...). Heuristic behaviour is the riskiest: it can be mistaken for real cause and effect.
kind_legend.information: Buys or shows information; changes no number of the quarter.
kind_legend.qualitative: Text or planning decisions; no known numeric effect.
kind_legend.scenario: An assumption the player chooses (rival behaviour). Results are conditional on it.

maturity_legend.heuristic: Practice rule from general business sense; no literature, no calibration. Lowest rung. Placeholder accounting rules (structure from game parameters, combination unverified) are heuristic too.
maturity_legend.literature: Functional form backed by published literature; coefficients not calibrated on this game.
maturity_legend.not-modeled: The real game has it; this engine does not.
maturity_legend.verified: Captured from the game and reproduced (or fitted on game data and passed hold-out validation).

rules: Structure and maturity only. No game values, no market data, no fitted coefficients.

real_status: measured = seen in the captured Q1 menu or reproduced by an experiment; inferred = a client screen is registered but was not seen in Q1, and/or a public teaching source describes it (unverified until captured); unknown = no evidence either way.
Anything inferred stays 'unverified, awaiting capture' until a later quarter is captured.
Downstream numbers always take the weakest maturity of their inputs.
